source: docs/v1-spec.md, Feasibility math. Starting defaults, user-overridable. Recalibrated 2026-10-29 against data/reference/test_parcels.csv (see docs/calibration-2026-10-29.md). Base costs are provisional until the partner contractor's actual job costs are in.

production.note: small-builder spec flats; evidence in docs/construction-costs-2026-10-29.md (Missing Middle awards, NAHB, test-set sales)

build_spec_presets.status: set from published evidence 2026-10-29 (docs/construction-costs-2026-10-29.md); replace with real job costs when available

escalation.series_name: Census constant-quality price index of new single-family houses under construction (Laspeyres, 2005 = 100)
escalation.table: cost_escalation_index (latest per series and 12-month change in view cost_escalation)
escalation.rule: preset x (latest census_uc / base_value), then x (1 + 12-month change) ^ (build months / 2 / 12) to reach the build midpoint; show base month, latest month and both changes
escalation.why: decision 23: the Census index prices whole houses (labor and margin included); PPI goods covers materials only and runs hotter (+9.7% vs +1.6% in the 12 months to September 2026), so it is shown as a signal, not applied

neighborhood_adjustment.rule: production preset only: 1 + 0.5 * (min(index, 1.3) - 1); standard and high presets: 1.0, because the same index already picks those presets (index 1.3 or more: standard, 1.8 or more: high)
neighborhood_adjustment.why: applying the adjustment to every preset counts the area twice: a Lincoln Park 3-flat (index 1.94) would cost $250 x 1.47 = $368 per sq ft. This is the rule the calibration used (scripts/research/2026-10-29/cal.py).
neighborhood_adjustment.index_caveat: permit reported costs are rough guesses (69% are exact multiples of $50,000) and the city's permit fee does not depend on them; use the index as a coarse ranking only

sprinklers_note: applies to the building with 4+ units; a detached coach house does not add the main building's count (verify against the 2026 code)

permit_fee.construction_factor_status: placeholder until confirmed from city fee tables

formula.base: cost_before_financing = land + hard + sprinklers + contingency + soft + permit
formula.note: computed on cost before financing, so there is no circular reference

reference_margin_on_cost.also_show: margin on revenue = profit / net sale

buyer_financing.display: financing class per scenario; flag whole-building price above the FHA limit

sell.target_note: 20% on cost; 15% is the low end of published benchmarks (RICS, PPG para 019). Show 15%, 20% and 25% reference lines and the margin on net sale. Decision 26, docs/research/decisions-2026-10-30.md

reference_tests.display: reference lines beside the result; never a pass/fail verdict

property_tax.line: explicit tax line; value = NOI before tax / (cap rate + effective tax rate)
property_tax.effective_tax_rate: from the Assessor and Clerk tax rate for the tax code, 1.52-2.0% typical
property_tax.source: CCAO cap rate policy 2023; Civic Federation; decision 31

rents.base: Census ACS 2020-2024 median gross rent by bedrooms (B25031), tract, then ZIP area, then the tract's overall median (B25064 for the all-units figure); keyless summary files, python -m jobs.load_rents
rents.growth: Zillow ZORI by ZIP from the ACS midpoint (2022-07) to the estimate date, as a ratio only; never displayed
rents.evidence: python -m jobs.check_rents, 2026-10-30: Assessor 2024 Chicago income worksheets (csik-bsws), potential gross income / 12 / units over the unit-mix ACS rent moved to 2024-01 with ZIP growth. 171 apartment buildings built 2014 or later: median 0.984, 10th-90th percentile 0.785-1.425 (56 low-rise: 0.928). 6,846 older buildings: 0.846. New buildings rent 16% above older ones on the same basis.
rents.why_below_the_old_premium: ACS gross rent includes utilities and the Assessor's income does not, so older buildings come in at 0.85 of ACS; new buildings land near ACS, 16% above older stock
rents.caveat: Assessor rents are the office's market estimates, not signed leases. Replace with a rent API or MRED leases when available.

margins_by_stage.applies_to: all cost lines except land; land is a known or entered price
margins_by_stage.why: ASTM E2516 / AACE class ranges and the Alberta estimate series put early-stage overruns above the original highs; kept until the contractor's job costs refit them (decisions 16-17, docs/research/decisions-2026-10-30.md)

sale_value_range.low: central x (1 + 10th percentile of leave-one-out errors)
sale_value_range.high: central x (1 + 90th percentile of leave-one-out errors)
sale_value_range.by: distance ring x kind (condo unit or whole building), refit nightly
sale_value_range.label: 80% range
sale_value_range.replaces: 25th-75th percentile of weighted comps, which covered 49% of test sales

sale_comps.pool: 2-6 unit buildings (class 211, x54s-btds) and condo units in 2-6 unit buildings (3r7i-mrz4) built 2014 or later, first arm's-length sale after construction (wvhk-k5uv)
sale_comps.search: same unit-count group within 0.75 mi, then 1.5 mi, then any unit count within 1.5 mi, then 3 mi, then citywide; at least 6 comps; sales within 3 years

time_adjustment.index: FHFA all-transactions HPI, Chicago-Naperville-Schaumburg metro division, annual mean of quarters; tract and ZIP loaded for testing
time_adjustment.note: public domain; can be shown on screen

rules: keep warranty, trustee and special warranty deeds; drop quit claim, other and executor deeds
drop a sale whose price repeats an earlier sale of the same PIN within 24 months
drop a sale below 50% of the weighted comp median per sq ft for its unit group (likely sold before completion)
use the Assessor sale_filter flags and is_multisale as published
filters.why: two of 37 test sales failed these checks on 2026-10-29 (data/reference/test_parcels_removed.csv)

sale_comps.kind: condo-unit scenarios use condo comps only; whole-building scenarios use both kinds (191 building comps are too few alone)

why.metro index: tract and ZIP indexes (FHFA, built from single-family loans) gave 15.0-15.4% holdout median error against 14.5% for metro; only 653 Cook tracts have a 2025 tract value
why.condo size only: building size elasticity 0.37 raised test-set error from 10.3% to 12.9% because unit sizes for planned buildings are defaults, not measured
why.3 years: 12.5% holdout median error against 13.7% at 4 years and 14.0% at 5 (IAAO allows up to 5 with time adjustment)
why.no blend: blend k=6 and k=12 gave 13.9-14.0% holdout median error and worse COD on buildings
why.condo to building 0.70: whole buildings sell for less per unit than condo units nearby: buildings estimated mostly from condo comps sold at 0.67 of the estimate. Fit on 129 building sales before 2025-07-01 (grid 0.65-1.0; 0.70 gave the lowest median error, 10.6%), then checked on the 61 holdout buildings (median error 11.7% to 10.1%, COD 40.1 to 24.8)

land_value_map.source: Germany Bodenrichtwerte and Singapore price per buildable area (docs/international-practices.md)
measures: land sale price per sq ft of lot
per sq ft moved to a 3,125 sq ft lot: price x (3125 / lot) ^ 0.858 / 3125
per buildable sq ft (lot area x FAR of the current district)
land_value_map.sales: vacant land (class 100, 190, 241) and teardowns (a residential building sale followed within 24 months by a demolition or new construction permit on the lot) in the last 36 months; same arm's-length checks as comps
land_value_map.unit: Assessor neighborhood; fall back to community area, then neighboring community areas
land_value_map.show: vacant and teardown medians separately and pooled, each with sale count and date range
land_value_map.teardown_source: McMillen and Singh, Land Value Estimation using Teardowns (Lincoln Institute); Dye and McMillen (2007), teardown prices approximate land value
land_value_map.job: python -m jobs.build_land_values (land_sale, land_value); 2026-10-30: 664 vacant and 407 teardown sales, 71 community areas

residual.name: residual land value (shown as max land price)
residual.formula: net sale / ((1 + target return) * (1 + finance share)) - cost before land and finance (exact solve; decision 25)
profit_shown_as: percent of net sale value (margin on value)
residual.existing_use_check: for parcels with a building: compare residual land value with existing-use value (Assessor market value from assessed value) and flag when residual is below it; owner may not sell at a price that works

show.high_case: central x (1 + high margin for the stage); about P90, not P80 (AACE ranges; a lognormal fit puts P80 near +19% when the high is +30%)

cost_confidence.refit: replace the stage margins with percentiles of actual overrun from users completed projects once 20 or more exist

cost_index_method.thin_areas: an area with fewer than 10 permits is blended with its neighboring community areas (community_area_neighbor): area weight n / 10, neighbors the rest. Changed 2026-10-30 from a side-of-city blend, to follow the neighborhood fallback in CLAUDE.md rule 4
cost_index_method.job: python -m jobs.build_cost_index (cost_index, cost_permit, permit_wait tables); 861 permits on 2026-10-30

fast_path.source: Japan by-right zoning, NSW complying development, Chicago self-certification
fast_path.definition: by-right units and floor area, no zoning relief, 1-8 units (self-certification eligible), not landmark, no demolition hold
fast_path.show: filter and badge with estimated weeks to permit

permit_duration.source: Chicago building permits ydr8-5enu, processing_time for the 836 permits behind the cost index
permit_duration.use: months of land carry before construction = days / 30; job recomputes monthly by review path
permit_duration.job: python -m jobs.build_cost_index writes permit_wait; 2026-10-30: self-cert median 48.5 days (p25 0, p75 94, 372 permits), standard plan review 83 (55, 161, 489)

open_space_impact_fee.formula: persons_by_unit_size x 87 sq ft per person x open_space_cost_per_sqft x 0.30, rounded per unit

open_space_cost_per_sqft.2028+: lesser of prior x Chicago CPI or 102.5%

open_space_impact_fee.exemptions: replacement unit with a demolition permit under one year old; credits for on-site open space
open_space_impact_fee.check: 2025 worksheet shows $418/$836/$1,254/$1,672, matching the formula at $16

range_method.method: seeded 10,000-draw Monte Carlo in the engine; sale errors from leave-one-out residuals, cost lognormal fit to the stage margins; show P10, P50, P90 and the share of draws with a loss
range_method.corner_case: low sale with high cost shown as 'stress case'
range_method.correlation_note: editable; 0 available as a toggle; no Chicago estimate exists
